what_it_measured.text: Measurements were all subjective; no objective testing was performed to verify their improvements.

dose.text: The dose of BPC 157 was 2 cc or 4 mg (2000 mcg/ml). The dose of BPC 157 with TB4 varied from a low dose of BPC157 of 2 mg (1 cc) and 3 mg (1 cc) of TB4 to a high dose of BPC 157 of 4 mg (2cc) combined with 6 mg (2cc) of TB4.

route.text: A 25 G 1.5-inch needle was inserted into the knee via the medial tibia plateau area and 2 cc of BPC 157 was injected into the knee joint.

endpoint.text: Patients were asked to rate their pain prior to injection, the length of time the peptides helped ease the pain and the degree to which the injection helped them. No specific tools were used to measure their improvement in function, quality of life, stiffness or activities of daily living. The survey’s main goal was to determine whether BPC157 helped with multiple types of knee pain in a primary care setting.

Patients were asked to rate their pain prior to injection, the length of time the peptides helped ease the pain and the degree to which the injection helped them. No specific tools were used to measure their improvement in function, quality of life, stiffness or activities of daily living. The survey’s main goal was to determine whether BPC157 helped with multiple types of knee pain in a primary care setting.
Of the patients who received both peptides, 75% showed significant improvement, but 25% had no relief of their knee pain.
